problem: Synthetic instruction generators for VLN data augmentation (e.g., the HM3D-AutoVLN speaker) produce low-quality, poorly grounded and low-diversity instructions, limiting the benefit of augmenting training data. Web-scale alternatives such as Airbert need very large numbers of environments.
motivation: Human instructions are costly to collect, so lack of annotated data is a key bottleneck for VLN. Better-quality and more diverse synthetic instructions for unlabeled HM3D trajectories should translate into better navigation agents.
key_idea: Train a GPT-2 instruction generator adversarially against a BERT discriminator (GAN-like, using Gumbel-Softmax), conditioning on image features plus detected object names, to produce diverse well-formed instructions for augmenting VLN training.
insight: Object-detection names in the input are critical: removing them drops val-unseen CIDEr from 0.486 to 0.132 and REVERIE SPL from 41.9 to 38.9. Adversarial fine-tuning makes instructions far more diverse and 100% novel (Div-2 0.210 vs GT 0.113), and slight description gains translate into navigation gains (+2.5 SPL over HM3D-AutoVLN* with the same DUET and paths). The medium variant trained from scratch (no adversarial pre-training) is 0.7 SPL worse.
method: Generator (GPT-2): flattens ResNet-152 image features of the trajectory frontal views plus Mask2Former (ADE20K) object-name tokens as a prompt, then autoregressively generates the instruction after BOS, with position and segment embeddings separating modalities
Discriminator (BERT): takes image features, object names and an instruction; FC+sigmoid outputs real/fake, trained with BCE
Adversarial training: L_G=-log D(I_G,x), L_D=-log(1-D(I_G,x))-log D(I_R,x); trained simultaneously; Gumbel-Softmax lets gradients pass through discrete sampled tokens
Data augmentation: generate one instruction per trajectory for 217K HM3D paths (same paths as AutoVLN)
Downstream: DUET pretrained on 4 auxiliary tasks following AutoVLN, then finetuned on REVERIE/R2R training splits augmented with the synthetic instructions

setting.backbone: GPT-2 decoder + BERT encoder discriminator (trained; ResNet-152 features, Mask2Former detections); downstream navigator DUET
setting.training_data: REVERIE ground-truth instructions on Matterport3D trajectories for AIGeN; 217K synthetic HM3D trajectory-instruction pairs added to DUET pretraining/finetuning
setting.observation: panoramic RGB (only frontal 60° view used for instruction generation) plus object detection labels; DUET uses panoramic views with topological map
setting.privileged: none at navigation test time; instruction generation uses Mask2Former detections of the last panoramic view of each trajectory

numbers.extra: 217K HM3D synthetic instructions from AIGeN added to pretraining/finetuning

results: DUET+AIGeN reaches REVERIE val-unseen SR 54.4, SPL 41.9, RGSPL 26.9, beating HM3D-AutoVLN* (SPL 39.4) and the DUET baseline (+8.2 SPL). On R2R it gets SPL 63/SR 73 on val-unseen and SPL 61/SR 71 on test-unseen, beating AZHP/KERM/HAMT on SPL.
limitations: Relies on Mask2Former object labels of the last panoramic view, which is time-consuming and needed for quality; without them performance drops
Uses only the frontal view of each panorama and is trained on REVERIE-style instructions, so instructions are often wrong on landmark or target object
Gains are evaluated only with one navigator (DUET) and one set of 217K trajectories
